about: The 4 humidity options, realistic model + smart controller, seasonal plan. RH numbers count only the hours with flowers inside.

date_range.label: 1 Jan 2026 – 6 Nov 2026 (310 days, real Visakhapatnam weather, digital twin)

note: Digital twin (S) on real 2026 Visakhapatnam weather. Nothing here is measured. E = assumption (config/design.json -> assumptions_E, data/crops.json, data/season_calendar.json).
best_why: highest Rs value of the flowers at take-out (E prices); ties go to the option that uses less water

rules.ethylene: No fruit in the room. Ripening fruit (banana, mango, tomato, papaya) gives off ethylene gas, which makes flowers open, drop petals and brown early.
rules.ethylene_source: UC Davis Postharvest; USDA Agriculture Handbook 66.
rules.water: Never spray water directly on the flowers: wet petals rot. Raise the room humidity instead (bags, fogger).
handling: Pick at bud stage, early in the morning.
Optional boric-acid dip (jasmine, tuberose) – about 2× life (E).
Keep the door closed at night.

faq_months.q: Can flowers be stored for months?
faq_months.a: No. Fresh loose flowers last 1–3 weeks at best (bagged, 2–7 °C). Only carnation buds at 0–1 °C with special treatment can last months. Our room is a 1–7 day holding room. For long-term value: jasmine concrete, marigold lutein/dye, rose gulkand, dried flowers.

E.humidity.liner_transpiration_factor: E – perforated polyethylene crate liners cut the water loss of the flowers to about 25 % of the unlined value (literature for perforated film liners: 50-90 % less weight loss).
E.humidity.tray: E – open water tray 0.5 m2 on the floor, natural convection 4 W/m2K (our estimate).
E.humidity.fogger: E – ultrasonic fogger 0.30 L/h, 30 W, switched on below 90 % RH and off at 95 % (design brief + typical small unit). Needs clean (RO) water.
E.humidity.flower_air_speed: E – air speed around the flowers 0.5 m/s with the cooler fan on, 0.1 m/s with it off (our estimate).
